messages.author: 6a50f393e991ef35
messages.subject: Re: Installing on Centos 6.5 with the latest R version on it...
parts:
Hi Guillermo,
Sorry you are having trouble. It's clear to me why you are getting that message. My first inclination is that there is a permissions issue, though I may be wrong.

In the output you posted in your message, I notice that their is a $ at your shell prompt which indicates that you are not running yum as the root user.
In line 1 of the CentOS install instructions it says:

  1. Log in as root or a user with sudo privileges. If the latter, precede commands requiring root privileges withsudo.

Please try to run the command as user root, or prefaced with sudo as the install doc suggests:
sudo yum --nogpgcheck localinstall RRO-8.0-Beta-el6.x86_64.rpm

Please report back the results you receive.

Thank you,
Chris Mosetick
Revolution Analytics

Hi, Guillermo

One possibility to manage multiple side by side installations of R (or any application, for that matter) is to use the Linux alternatives command.

This command allows you create and manage symbolic links to the different installations, and thus easily refer to the installation of your choice.

See for example http://linux.die.net/man/8/alternatives
